info.bio:
Raw Power is an Italian Hardcore Punk band formed in 1981 by Mauro and Giuseppe Codeluppi (voice and guitar). Since the beginning the band had great troubles finding a stable line-up. As a matter of fact, the only two members still in the band from the original line-up are the two founders-brothers.

The vinyl debut LP "You Are The Victim" was released in 1983 through a small independent Italian label. In 1983 the band signed a deal with American indie-punk label Toxic Shock (Skin Yard, House Of Large Sizes.

scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El punk como «violento, rápido y ruidoso» tarda en conquistar EE UU, pero cuando lo hace el hardcore se convierte durante dos décadas en el idioma nacional de millones de chavales. Misfits y el «scum-rock»; el crossover punk-metal (Suicidal Tendencies, Corrosion Of Conformity, Agnostic Front); Mission Of Burma en Boston. Washington: Bad Brains (reggae, funk y metal diez años por delante), Minor Threat (el «straight-edge») y Rites Of Spring, inventores del emo-core. San Francisco: Dead Kennedys de Jello Biafra, D.R.I. (thrash antes que Metallica), Flipper. Los «beach punks» de Los Ángeles: Germs, X, Black Flag (Damaged), Descendents, Gun Club (Fire Of Love), Bad Religion. El jazz-core de Minutemen y Saccharine Trust; en el Medio Oeste, Husker Du y Replacements cambian el hardcore para siempre; en Chicago, Naked Raygun y Big Black de Steve Albini; en Europa, The Ex y los italianos CCCP.

xref.title: Bowie's Admiration and Support
xref.body: David Bowie considered Iggy Pop one of his musical heroes, captivated by Iggy's craziness, mental instability, and intelligence that Bowie saw beyond the drug use and wild stage persona. Bowie became Iggy's patron, securing funding for The Stooges' *Raw Power* album. When Iggy eventually ended up in a mental hospital after the band's collapse, Bowie was his only visitor. "Bowie saw that Iggy was actually very, very intelligent."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Bowie's Intervention and *Raw Power* Production
xref.body: David Bowie, then on a hot streak with significant industry power, bonded with Iggy Pop. He convinced Iggy, Ron and Scott Ashton, and James Williamson to move to England to record *Raw Power* for Columbia Records, effectively resurrecting the band. "Bowie was on a hot streak and thus he had power. And after bonding with Iggy, he convinced him, the Ashton brothers in James Williamson, to come to England where they'd all make a record for Columbia Records."

xref.title: Major Influence in American Hardcore
xref.body: Hüsker Dü was a major influence in American hardcore, distinguishing themselves by combining the raw power and energy of hardcore with melody and more conventional song structures. They sometimes incorporated instruments like piano and acoustic guitars, representing a huge evolutionary leap for punk music. "In the history of American hardcore, they were a major influence."

xref.title: Patronage of Iggy Pop and The Stooges
xref.body: Bowie was a great admirer and musical hero of Iggy Pop, fascinated by his craziness, almost constant mental instability, and ability to see beyond the drugs and self-destructive stage antics to Iggy's intelligence. Bowie convinced his manager to take on Iggy and The Stooges as a project, providing a cash injection that funded their *Raw Power* album. He later visited Iggy when he was in a mental hospital. Bowie's acceptance of Iggy also helped propel the first three Stooges albums to become important templates for punk rock. "Iggy's craziness had made him into one of Bowie's musical heroes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Savior of The Stooges
xref.body: Leveraging his influence and industry power, David Bowie convinced Iggy Pop and the Ashton brothers, along with James Williamson, to move to England to record the *Raw Power* album for Columbia Records, effectively restarting The Stooges' career. "Bowie, although not in the greatest shape himself when it came to drugs, turned out to be Iggy's and ultimately the studio's savior."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Shift from Raw Speed to Polished Sound
xref.body: Before "The Black Album," Metallica was known for "raw speed and raw power." However, with the 1991 album, producer Bob Rock guided them to "slow down a bit and polished up their sound," a move that angered speed metal purists but significantly broadened their appeal. "Now up until this record, Metallica was all about raw speed and raw power."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Sound Blending Speed with Melody
xref.body: Their music was characterized by its loud and fast nature, yet it consciously incorporated elements of basic pop songs. Melody and traditional song structure were given equal importance alongside the raw power and volume, pushing the boundaries of what was considered punk. "And although their music was loud and fast, the songs incorporated elements of a basic pop song."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
